# Code Review — 2026-08-12

- Repo: `danieljustus/symaira-appkit` (SPM Swift library, macOS 14+/iOS 17+, Swift 6)
- HEAD: `2c8d2c1`; cycle commits since parent base `6d4645b`: only `2c8d2c1` (Dependabot actions bump — no source changes this cycle), so the review targets the current main state.
- Follow-up to review 2026-08-06 (`b446d3a`): re-verified each prior finding against current source. Still open: redaction gaps (being fixed this cycle), Keychain access control, UpdateApplier size + in-memory download. Stale/not re-flagged: FormComponentsTests `@MainActor` warnings (no such warnings in the current test build), SymairaMCP README gap (Modules table still lacks it — fixed this cycle as trivial).

## Findings

- [ ] **[Security] Redaction misses provider-prefixed token shapes (GitHub/Slack/Stripe/AWS/JWT)**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaCLIRunner/CLIRunner.swift:110-139` redacts via length-based patterns: base64 `[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,}`, hex `{32,}`, key-value prefixes. Real-world tokens with structural separators escape: `ghp_`+36 chars (underscore breaks the run; 36 < 40), `github_pat_…`, `xoxb-…`, `sk_live_…` (the secret tail is ~24 chars < 40), `AKIA…` key ids (16 chars), and dotted JWT segments (header segment is 36 chars; base64url `-`/`_` break the class). The existing JWT test (`CLIRunnerTests.swift:139`) only passes because its fixture omits the dots.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add explicit provider-shape patterns ahead of the length-based ones: `gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`, `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}`, `xox[baprs]-\S+`, `sk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]+`, `(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}`, and a three-segment JWT `eyJ\S*\.\S*\.\S*`. Extend the test fixture with a real dotted JWT and a `ghp_` token (assembled at runtime via concatenation so the literal never sits in source — GitHub push protection blocks format-valid dummies).
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact. **Being fixed in this cycle's PR with tests.**

- [ ] **[Security] `SymairaKeychain` has no optional access-control (passcode/biometry) enforcement**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaKeychain/SymairaKeychain.swift:49-57` stores items with `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`; any process running as the user can read them once the Mac is unlocked. For high-value secrets (API tokens) there is no way to require user presence.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add an optional `accessControl` API (e.g. `save(_:key:requireUserPresence: Bool)`) backed by `SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags` with `kSecAccessControlDevicePasscode` (or `biometryCurrentSet` with passcode fallback). Default stays as today — backward compatible for existing consumers.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact.

- [ ] **[Performance] `UpdateApplier` buffers the entire release asset in memory; size guard fires only after the fact**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/UpdateApplier.swift:1088-1137` (`downloadToTemp`) uses `client.data(for:)`, so the full asset — up to `maxAssetBody = 1 GiB` (line 488) — sits in memory before the size check at line 1105 can reject it. An oversized or endless response is only detected after it has been fully buffered. Progress is reported once at 100% (line 1134), so the progress callback is useless during the download.
  - **Proposed solution:** Stream the response to the temp file (`URLSession.AsyncBytes` or delegate-based writes), check `expectedContentLength` against `maxAssetBody` *before* reading the body, abort when the running count exceeds the cap, hash incrementally (`SHA256` supports streaming updates), and call `progress?` per chunk.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact.

- [ ] **[Architecture] `UpdateApplier.swift` keeps growing as a 1163-line multi-responsibility module**
  - **Status quo:** `Sources/SymairaUpdateCheck/UpdateApplier.swift` (1163 lines, up from ~800 at the last review) handles checksum manifest parsing, cosign verification, download, DMG and ZIP install paths, Homebrew install-method detection, and rollback — all as private methods on one type. Hard to navigate; new features (DMG install landed since) keep accreting here.
  - **Proposed solution:** Extract focused internal helpers along the existing seams: `ChecksumManifest` parsing, `AssetDownloader` (see the streaming finding), `CosignVerifier`, `AppInstaller` (DMG/ZIP/Volume-swap). Keep `UpdateApplier` as the orchestrator; no public API change.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact.

- [ ] **[UX/DX] README Modules table omits the `SymairaMCP` module**
  - **Status quo:** `README.md:24-31` documents seven products; `SymairaMCP` (added in #59, shipped since 0.9.0) is missing from the table, so consumers can't discover `MCPServer`/`MCPTransport`/`MCPTypes` from the README.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add a `SymairaMCP` row (one line, matching the existing style).
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact. **Being fixed in this cycle's PR.**

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Issue-template contact link points at disabled GitHub Discussions**
  - **Status quo:** `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` links "Symaira Community" to the repo's Discussions tab, but Discussions is disabled on the repo (`hasDiscussionsEnabled: false`) — reporters hit a dead page.
  - **Proposed solution:** Remove the `contact_links` block, keeping `blank_issues_enabled: false` (or enable Discussions — a repo-settings decision for the owner).
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / low impact. **Being fixed in this cycle's PR (file-side fix).**

## Conclusion

The codebase is in good shape: subprocess timeouts, output caps, redaction plumbing and the schema handshake are all in place, and the previous cycle's coverage work held (87.4%, delta 0). Quick win already underway: the redaction patterns for provider-prefixed tokens plus the two trivial doc fixes ship in this cycle's PR. The two structural items worth issues are the `UpdateApplier` streaming download and the Keychain access-control option.
